scenes.title: Kahneman and Tversky flipping the +3,000 Gain Card vs -3,000 Loss Card beside the asymmetric Prospect Theory S-curve
scenes.era: 1979, Jerusalem / Stanford behavioral decision seminar room

layout.description: Sunlit 1979 university seminar room with a warm wooden table holding two large printed choice placards ('Problem 3: +3,000 Sure vs 80% +4,000' and 'Problem 4: -3,000 Sure vs 80% -4,000') in front of a chalkboard drawn with the famous asymmetric S-shaped Value Function.

positions.who: Amos Tversky (mannequin in 1970s open-collar shirt and rolled sleeves)
positions.where: standing at the chalkboard tracing the steep downward Loss curve dropping twice as fast below the center origin as the gentle Gain curve rises above

positions.who: Daniel Kahneman (mannequin in 1970s blazer and glasses)
positions.where: turning over Problem Card 4 on the wooden table to reveal 92% switching from safe choice to risky gamble
pointing in astonishment from their cautious '+3,000' check mark to their opposite '-4,000 gamble' check mark

props.name: paired Gain (+3,000) vs Loss (-3,000) placard cards
props.period_detail: two crisp white tabletop placards showing identical probabilities with flipped signs
props.physical_behavior: expose the 80%-safe to 92%-risky reversal on one table

props.name: asymmetric S-curve chalkboard graph
props.period_detail: crisp white chalk axes ('Gains / Losses' horizontal, 'Psychological Value' vertical) where the lower-left loss cliff plunges 2x steeper than the upper-right gain hill

props.name: ceramic university coffee mug
props.period_detail: plain ceramic mug resting at the reference-point origin

actions.verb_sequence: slides down the '+3,000 Sure' placard where 80% raise hands -> flips over the '-3,000 Sure' placard and watches 92% switch hands to the 80% -4,000 gamble
taps the chalk Reference Point at (0,0) and draws the 2x-steeper drop into the loss quadrant

reactions.reaction: laughs catching their own brain reversing completely over a single minus sign

scenes.wardrobe: 1979 academic attire: open-collar Oxford shirt, light tweed blazer, corduroy trousers.
scenes.lighting: Warm high-key Mediterranean / California seminar daylight.
scenes.recognition_hook: Change one plus sign into a minus sign on the exact same math problem, and 80 percent cautious savers turn into 92 percent desperate gamblers.

key_visual.description: two 1979 psychologists at a seminar table flipping +3,000 vs -3,000 choice placards in front of a chalkboard drawn with an asymmetric S-shaped Prospect Theory curve

scenes.title: Thaler's university coffee-mug ownership split

layout.description: Sunlit lecture row where every second desk has a new ceramic university mug placed on it.

positions.where: cradling the ceramic mug protectively writing '7.00' on a valuation slip
glancing casually at the identical mug writing '3.50' on an offer slip

props.name: identical ceramic university mugs & valuation slips
props.physical_behavior: five minutes of ownership doubles valuation

actions.verb_sequence: hands mugs to random half of row -> collects written value slips showing 2-to-1 split

scenes.recognition_hook: Five minutes of owning a simple coffee mug doubles the price your brain demands to let it go.

scenes.title: 90% Survival vs 10% Mortality medical framing card

layout.description: Clean conference table where two clinicians read identical surgical statistics printed in '90% One-Month Survival' vs '10% One-Month Mortality' booklets.

positions.who: Two Clinician mannequins in white coats

props.name: paired '90% Survival' vs '10% Mortality' cards
props.physical_behavior: shift surgical approval dramatically even among doctors

actions.verb_sequence: places both booklets side-by-side realizing 90% survival and 10% mortality describe the exact same surgery

scenes.recognition_hook: Even trained doctors recommend surgery far more often when the exact same odds say '90% survive' instead of '10% die.'

scenes.title: Resetting a sunk-cost project to 'Fresh Zero Today'

layout.description: Bright modern desk where a founder covers up the 'Past Hours Spent' column with a blank white card reading 'Starting From Zero Today: Would We Build This?'

positions.where: placing the clean 'Zero Today' card over the sunk-loss column and calmly closing the stalled project binder

props.name: clean 'Zero Today' reference card
props.physical_behavior: frees the team from chasing a -3,000 loss gamble

actions.verb_sequence: covers past sunk hours -> evaluates future upside cleanly -> pivots to the stronger project

scenes.recognition_hook: Resetting your mental reference point to 'starting fresh today' breaks sunk-cost gambling.
